title: The Imperishable Record, Forgiveness, and the Future of Criminal Justice
abstract: arXiv:2610.15499v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Digital technologies can preserve records of wrongdoing indefinitely, and AI can give those records continuing influence over a person's future. We describe this condition as the eternal data present and argue that it threatens the possibility of forgiveness. In criminal justice, formal punishment has an end, whereas the harms caused by the continued use of criminal records may not. Drawing on Hegel's account of the "hard heart" and Arendt's account of the irreversibility of action, we distinguish two dangers that digital systems can combine. People may be permanently identified with what they have done, and acts that cannot be undone may continue to determine what happens to them. We propose a right to remain unfinished, supported by rights to limits on the weight given to older records, to re-evaluation in light of personal change, to reassessment of inferences that affect their lives, and to time limits on the use of records in spec

translated_title: 不朽的记录、宽恕与刑事司法的未来
translated_abstract: 数字技术可以无限期地保存不当行为的记录，而人工智能可以让这些记录持续影响一个人的未来。我们将这种状况描述为“永恒的数据当下”，并论证它威胁着宽恕的可能性。在刑事司法中，正式惩罚有一个终点，而持续使用犯罪记录所造成的伤害却可能没有尽头。借鉴黑格尔关于“硬心肠”的论述和阿伦特关于行动不可逆转性的论述，我们区分了数字系统可能叠加的两种危险：人们可能被永久地等同于他们曾经的所作所为，而无法撤销的行为可能持续决定着他们的命运。我们提出一种“保持未完成状态的权利”，该权利由以下几项权利支撑：对旧记录所占比重加以限制的权利、根据个人变化获得重新评估的权利、对影响自身生活的推论进行重新审视的权利，以及对记录使用设定时间限制的权利。
tldr: 论文指出数字技术与AI造就的“永恒数据当下”会将人永久等同于过去的过错并威胁宽恕的可能性，因而提出以“保持未完成状态的权利”（包括限制旧记录权重、重新评估、审视推论和时限）重塑刑事司法的未来。
en_tdlr: The paper argues that the "eternal data present" created by digital technologies and AI threatens forgiveness by permanently tying people to past wrongs, and proposes a "right to remain unfinished" for the future of criminal justice.
